text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Empire Game [[VIDEOID:8f653ee987e2df8b52e209e097da8a22]] This is such a cool game! It's a scaled down version of Monopoly, and each game only takes 5-15 minutes to play, instead of the hours of a regular Monopoly game. So you'll hear something with this Monopoly game that you won't hear with any other Monopoly game, which is "Want to play again?"

It still captures the essence of Monopoly, so it still feels like a Monopoly game. It's more of a social game than a strategy game, but that will make it more fun for more people.

They've taken out the property cards, and replaced them with little tiles and a tower. The number of tiles, not the original value of the tile, determine how much that you pay when you land on someone else's property. The old Community Chest cards are now Empire cards, and you get a couple to hold on to at the start of the game, and you can use these strategically, and do various combos with them.

It's very fun, and I liked it a lot. If you get just one game this year, this should be the game you pick.

Pros:
+Excellent instructions
+Extremely well designed
+Has cool brands like Fender, Nerf, and Coke
+Quick version of Monopoly (I never thought I'd ever use quick and Monopoly in the same sentence.)
+They did an awesome job of play testing this game. It's very balanced and very fun. Whoever worked on the team that made this game should be promoted.

Cons:
-Less strategy than regular Monopoly, but it is more fun for more people
-Because it's subsidized by advertising, they really should be giving this game away. But, the advertising isn't as annoying as in other games.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Empire Game

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Oh My Gourd! Family Game for Boys & Girls Age 6 & Up - A Fun & Fast Family Game You Can Play Over & Over This game is best for really young children! I'd say 2-4. My son is almost 4, but he has some learning delays, so this game has proved perfect for him. Most of the games that are sold in stores, like Wal-Mart are still too old for him. I believe in challenging him, but he just doesn't understand them yet. Again, though, this one has proved to be perfect for him. I've already ordered another game from this line, with hopes to add more along.

There's no type of competition with it. There's 6 wooden snails, a race-board, and two dice. You roll the dice and whatever color they land on, you move that colored snail up a space. If both dice land on the same color, you move that colored snail 2 spaces. Sometimes, I had to wonder what the point was! It IS a great learning tool, though. It teaches taking turns, learning colors, and counting. Plus, quality learning time with children is always a good thing.

While I received this one free for review, I honestly would have purchased it. Before I received it, I didn't even know about this line of games. My son has had fun with it, and I'm really glad that it's now part of our game collection.

Overall, I'd say if your child is very young, or has learning delays, or simply likes simple games, this is a great choice. If your child is used to more advanced games, I wouldn't bother with it. There looks to be more advanced, yet still educational games from this line that might be a better choice, though.

Hasbro Bop It Bounce This is the modern version of a game in which you get an electronic paddle, a ball and you can bounce, and it counts the number of bounces and you get an announcer to say it. My nephew enjoyed playing with this little gadget. The voice command cues you through six different games: 1. MAX BOUNCE - You have 30 seconds to bounce the ball and seeing how many times you can bounce it. 2. INFINITY BOUNCE - Just keep on bouncing. 3. HANG TIME - Catch as many air as you can in 5 bounces. 4. RIGHT HEIGHT - The game calls the shots, whether to hit the ball high or low. 5. LITTLE-MIDDLE-BIG - Hit it high, middle or low. 6. FREE FORM - Freestyle bouncing.

I recommend playing outside the house and it is fascinating for young and old. Sometimes when I am tired of reading or watching TV, I play this for few minutes to take my mind off. It is a lot of fun.

text_fidelity_a: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath This is a perfect addition to the Fall basket. There are always lots of books about squirrels and acorns to add to the fall line-up and this game goes with them well. It's a great companion to those books and we've all had fun with it. There's also a little puzzle to go with the game, which adds more fun to the squirrel/acorn focus. To play the game, the players take turns rolling a die. The color/number that is rolled is what color and how many(up to 2) acorns you put into Charlie's mouth. Once he gets full, the acorns roll out the holes that are in the tree trunk that Charlie stands on. Using only one hand, the players race to collect the acorns. The first player to fill up their acorn stash card wins. The rules say that if a player rolls a certain color and it's not in the main stash of acorns, that player has to take one of their collected acorns or take one from another player. Taking from another player won't be for all families, but it can be adapted, if desired. Also, with the acorns rolling everywhere, it's tricky finding the best place to play. The acorns will roll off the table, but if on the floor, they could roll under things, like couches, if it's a smaller space. Our home is small, so we try to put up little "walls" to make sure the acorns don't roll under things. Overall, it's a fun game and the quality of it is nice, too. It's a simple game that's a great way to add a bit of joy to a day.
text_fidelity_b: Chompin' Charlie Game - Feed The Squirrel Acorns And Race To Collect Them When They Scatter - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath

Hasbro Gaming Yippie Yippie Yeti Game We just aren't overly fond of this game. It ended up being super frustrating for us.

When you first open the game, you have to put the game board together. This takes a bit of time, but it's not too bad. It looks nice enough, and I like that the game board is thick and sturdy. My boys love the whole idea of the game, and I don't think we've ever played a game where the board stood up. That was really cool! Our biggest issue is how difficult it is to keep the climbers in place. They're constantly falling when they shouldn't be. My children are 3, 5, and 8, so that may have a great deal to do with it. Keeping those climbers hanging where they should proved impossible for us, though. It's also a little frustrating that each player has to move around to play. The game board only faces one way, and you can't move it without making the climbers fall off(even more). That means when 4 people are playing, you can't just sit in a spot and enjoy the game. You have to move around, depending on whose turn it is. That might not be a big deal for many, but it frustrated my little guys.

Overall, we really like the whole idea of the game, and the fact that the game board stands up, but it ended up being incredibly frustrating for everyone.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Yippie Yippie Yeti Game

text_fidelity_a:
Ninja Warrior Obstacle Course for Kids - 2X50FT Double Ninja Slackline with Most Complete Accessories for Kids, Swing, Trapeze Swing, Rope Ladder, Obstacle Net Plus 1.2M Arm Trainer I am hoping to upgrade my rating to 4-5 stars after my 9 year old has had time to play on this a few times. A few initial thoughts:

The instructions included were not great, I had to find a YouTube video and watch it a few times to figure out assembly. I’m not the engineering type and no, it’s not hard, but it still took me multiple tries to get it right.

After finally getting it set up, we realized the obstacles were still too far apart for my child. However, the tension is way too tight once it’s locked and loaded so you can’t just easily slide the metal bracket things. Which means you have to loosen the entire ratchet thing and basically start over again. We did this a few times which is a bit frustrating. It definitely takes some trial and error and if you have an excited and antsy kid who can’t wait to get on this thing, it makes it even more stressful.

My 9 year old is a bit tall and during the trial and error period we realized it was too low, so then I had to go get the big ladder and shimmy the slack lines up another 2 feet on both trees. Everything added together just took a lot of time.

That being said, everything looks well made and durable at this point. I still need to make a few adjustments so that hopefully she can play on it this weekend. We will then decide whether to keep this thing or not. The monkey grip is tough and the cargo net is super swingy so it’s tough, she said. We are not planning to use the swing but we did buy a separate wheel thing from the same company.

I do plan on installing the lower slack line, I think that will help her move from obstacle to obstacle while also working her core at the same time. Hoping to provide an update in a week or so.
text_fidelity_b: Ninja Warrior Obstacle Course for Kids - 2X50FT Double Ninja Slackline with Most Complete Accessories for Kids, Swing, Trapeze Swing, Rope Ladder, Obstacle Net Plus 1.2M Arm Trainer

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Deluxe Turntable Scrabble Remarkable. Scrabble is cool. Hep. Rad. Outta sight. But Scrabble in this deluxe form is sublime, intoxicating. The pieces stay put, thanks to little walls around each space. You can spin the board so as to not need to examine it upside down. The pieces never slide around. The plastic coating lets you wipe it off, unlike the cardboard version which stains. Nothing is compromised from the original, flat cardboard version, but everything is improved.

OK. Not everything. It still can't help you dump the Q, Z and J at the end of the game without a U. And it is unlikely to assist you in stopping your grandmother's amazing ability to squeeze you out of that triple word score you hoped to grab with a seven-letter word. Take that up with Gram. Just remember who made you the cookies.

Seriously, I recommend this to any family or commited Scrabble player. Families need it for that `full-body contact' style of play that sometimes happens with children or cats involved. Commited Scrabble players need it for pretty much the same reason!

I fully recommend this game.

Anthony Trendl
editor, HungarianBookstore.com
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Deluxe Turntable Scrabble

text_fidelity_a: Brainwaves: The Astute Goose - A Kosmos Game from Thames & Kosmos | Fun, Scientist Approved, Family-Friendly Games to Sharpen Your Mind & Train Your Brain, for Ages 8+ This card game can be played solo or with up to five players. It is intended for ages eight and up. The large cards are easy to hold and the things you're supposed to memorize on each card are clear to see. There are 25 suspect cards which include variations in color, clothing, and animals. You place three to six of these cards out (depending on the difficulty level you desire) and memorize each card before turning them upside down. There are six number cards that you place above each suspect so that you know which suspect to talk about when you roll the dice. The dice roll tells you which suspect to talk about and which feature (color, clothing, or animal) that you need to remember correctly for that suspect. If the player is able to correctly remember that feature, they keep the card and score a point, but if they remember wrong, the rest of the players each have a chance to guess until someone gets it right or no one does. That suspect card is replaced with a new one, and everyone has a chance to look at the new card. Thus, you are constantly having to remember new information for each position. This can be a fun way to train your brain to remember better, but some people might find it too frustrating.
text_fidelity_b: Brainwaves: The Astute Goose - A Kosmos Game from Thames & Kosmos | Fun, Scientist Approved, Family-Friendly Games to Sharpen Your Mind & Train Your Brain, for Ages 8+

QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits This is not a “puzzle”, but a “model”. I can only assume that they do not have a word for “model” in Chinese. Because Chinese companies always list items like this is a “puzzle” though it’s really not.

This model is made of wood. It shows to have 47 pieces. There are 3 boards with the cutout pieces. You’ll want to use caution when removing the pieces from the boards so that you do not break them. You remove the pieces from the boards as you go. The pieces are numbered on the instruction sheet, but not on the boards. So if you remove them all at 1st, it will make it very difficult to put the model together. I highly recommend you have either a razor blade or thin sharp knife available to help remove the pieces. If you simply use your fingers, you could easily break a piece.

I must admit that I am not a person who likes to build models. So it took me about an hour and ½ to put this together. It turned out okay, but not as perfect as the pictures. The shingles do not fit perfectly. Nonetheless I think it looks okay.

Also, when you get to pieces 12, 13, 14 and 15 which is part of instruction number 5… Those 4 pieces make a little platform. The way the instruction show it on instruction number 9, that platform sits inside section B. But if you place it there, then the top shingle portion sits on top of the platform and is not sturdy. If you don’t put that platform there, then the top piece see fits in to the bottom piece a which makes it sturdy. Then I use that platform as a base on the bottom to place the temple on top of. Written on that platform is “Temple of Serenity”. So because of that, I think it should go on the bottom is a base anyway. But of course you can do it anyway you want to.

An optional string of LED lights is included. Two AA batteries are required and not included.

As a bonus, there is also a small “Ellie House” which is 24 pieces.

This model is made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 30 bucks I think it is a bit expensive, but it is a unique and interesting item. Also, it comes in a nice cardboard box, which makes it easy for wrapping if you’re giving it as a gift.
text_fidelity_b: QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Krypt Gold 631 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - 15152 - Every Piece is Unique, Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly This was my first puzzle of this brand. While the pieces did fit together well, I noticed several pieces that out of the box had pegs that were bent, or paper lifting. While it didnt interfere with the puzzle assembly it just made the completed puzzle look ragged.

I suggest labeling the puzzle map to orient a "top" or "bottom" as during assembly you may accidently turn your map upside down.

Organizing the pieces is what I found most helpful by size, shape, and if has a curve/turn or not. Then when you reach a portion of the puzzle that you need, you can brute force from your pile.

Several pieces are very unique, and thus can serve as anchors to build off of.

The hardest part is the border, something I usually do first, as the pieces do not interlock on the edges, you have to do another layer in in order to interlock the edge pieces. Once I put the pieces in piles of similar size/shape, the puzzle assembly speed went much faster.

Took me about 20-25 hours total.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Krypt Gold 631 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - 15152 - Every Piece is Unique, Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly

text_fidelity_a:
My Little Pony Equestria Girls Twilight and Spike [[VIDEOID:4ac7ba54c290a47a623bdcdbf7740f53]] This is an excellent My Little Pony doll and puppy. At first I was confused, because I didn't know that My Little Ponies could take human form. I did some research, and the Equestria Girls series was when something was out of balance in the human world, and so Twilight Sparkle, the main pony, jumps through a magic mirror and turns into a human. Her sidekick dragon comes too, and he transforms into a puppy. Somehow they save the day by throwing a pajama party.

I was really impressed with how many points of articulation that the Twilight Sparkle doll has. You'll be able to pose her into whatever position that you want to. She comes with a pajama dress, with bloomers, with two shoes, and with a mask. Spike the puppy doesn't move at all, but he comes with a pajama hat.

As a side note, Twilight Sparkle doesn't have anything to do with the vampire books.

Pros:
+You can pose the doll in a ton of different positions
+High quality clothing
+Her hair is very nice for doll hair
+Fun and exciting

Cons:
-The box doesn't have any instructions or background on why the pony is in human form
-Twilight Sparkle can't stand on her own, but this is typical for dolls like this
text_fidelity_b: My Little Pony Equestria Girls Twilight and Spike

text_fidelity_a:
AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card [[VIDEOID:3ab25a1fe74e640fbb16d3764ecc8aea]] This Kid's Action Camera was better than I expected. The camera (not in the waterproof case) measures 2.5" tall x 2.25" wide x 7/8" thick. The full color screen on the back measures 1.5" tall x 1.25" wide. The photographs can be up to 5M (you select can 5M, 3M, 2M, or 1M), and the photographs actually look pretty good (good color balance, no distortion, in focus). You can record just audio, and this came out clear when the camera was held within a foot distance of my mouth. I didn't test any further. The video can be selected at 1080P, 720P, or VGA quality. The 1080P looked good but it doesn't appear to be the normal HD proportions but rather closer to a square than a long rectangle. Some of the recordings also had mysterious sounds in addition to the expected ones--maybe like something tapped against the case during the recording. Also, I haven't found a way to remove the automatic time stamp placed on the video and photos. You can playback the videos, etc. on the camera if desired and also delete them off if the take was a bad one.

I found the camera very easy to use once I read the instructions. One rechargeable Li-ion battery is included. You charge the battery using the included USB cord connected to a computer or using a USB charging adapter. There's a red LED light when charging which turns off when it's full. Charging didn't take long, and they estimate that a full charge from near empty will take about 2.5 hours. I did notice that, even with the camera switched off in addition to being turned off, the battery tends to drain. We used the camera a bit, then left it sitting for a few weeks, only to discover that it needed to be fully recharged before we could use it again. So just charge it periodically so it'll always have enough of a charge.

They estimate that you can take about 90 minutes of 1080P video on the included 32 GB micro SD card (probably limited by the battery as I think 32GB can hold twice that). You need to format the micro SD card before use. You can do this by inserting the card into the camera, going to the settings menu, and selecting the option to format the card. You can download the images, audio, and video from the camera either through the USB cable (turn the camera on before connecting to your computer) or by removing the micro SD card and inserting it in the destination computer.

The set includes connectors that allow you to connect the camera to connectors that attach to a helmet, a bike, and so on. In the instructions, they show how the various connectors can be used for different situations. The set also comes in a very nice storage / carrying case so the unused connectors and such don't get lost. There is a holder for the camera that is a waterproof shell (good up to 30m or 98 feet underwater) and this can also be connected to all these other connectors.

I tried to film a sunset, and it did look pretty accurate when the lens was pointed directly at the sun/brightest area. If I dropped the focus of the camera to the ground, the camera Auto changed things so that it looked like a bright daylight scene. I tried some video of moving objects (like a flag on a windy day) or with me moving the camera, and it came out good.

The 3 games were pretty simple and may bore kids used to touchscreens. For example, the puzzle game would be pretty quick to work except you have to select a piece, use the arrow to move it one square, then select a piece, etc. Lots of clicking the buttons. Still, fun if there aren't other options around.
text_fidelity_b: AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card

Klutz Crystal Unicorn Craft & Science Kit Crytal kits are notoriously iffy - sometimes they work, and sometimes they don't - and even the same kit will work sometimes, and not others. It has to be perfect, and I mean really perfect, for them to work at all.

For us, we ended up with crystals on only the base of the unicorn's tail and mane, and not on the tips (go figure). Those crystals are white or clear, and they look exactly like what they are - white crystals on a colored unicorn - not pink and blue crystals as the image on the box indicates.

Add to that the fact that there's roughly 1/3 of the items you'll need to make the kit included (you'll provide scissors, ruler, mason jars, distilled water, and a weight for the unicorn once you realize that it doesn't float), and this is a mediocre buy at best.

I was a little surprised by the material of the mat-- I thought the listing showed a three layered mat, but the one I received is only one layer, and it is a water resistant canvas type material. It's actually better this way, because often you need to be on a flat surface to have lego structures be able to stand independently. If the mat was too cushy it may make lego structures fall and be frustrating to work on top of, which would defy the whole point of having this easy cleanup basket! The mat attaches to the basket via velcro so you can use it together or separately (you don't need to have a basket attached to the mat while you're playing on it, for example). Makes cleanup so easy! I also like that you can throw the mat in the washing machine if that's the easiest way to clean up other things that may have gotten on there (like juice).

The basket itself is a canvas grey color, which fits in well with my couches (similar in color). The bright yellow mat, I feel draws kids to it, makes them excited to play, so it was a good choice overall.

There are still some little blue clippy things that came in the boxes that we never did figure out how to use, and I couldn't find the information anywhere on their website or google searches. Thames & Kosmos Lost Cities: Rivals Card Game | Strategy Auction Adventure | Vibrant Colors for Two to Four Players | Family Friendly Fun by Kosmos This is the third major rendition of the "Lost Cities" games (the card game, the board game, and now Rivals). Each is a game that is ostensibly about discovering lost cities, but is really about putting numbered cards in order. None are special games in my collection, although I now own all three, and all are well-loved by some gamers in the world. Rivals is potentially the most interesting of them, as it introduces a new auction mechanic into the standard put-numbers-in-order formula, but while I found this auction to be a new and interesting method of getting cards, the two other people who I've played it with are not convinced that it's fun so much as it's mean.

I think if you don't mind a game where you play one on one and directly attack others, then this might be something you can handle. I believe that while the others are light-hearted and super easy for anyone to pick up, this suffers from the "meanness" problem, and also from the fact that the more experienced player will easily dispatch newcomers. As many who love Lost CIities have a partner in mind for when they play, and tend not to play with outsiders, this may not be a problem for Rivals, but this is certainly more intense of a "game" than those, and is not always the light hearted fare that the old classics tend to be.

If you want a light, non-interactive card game, then the other Lost Cities are better choices. If you need something more interesting, then this is a good chocie.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Lost Cities: Rivals Card Game | Strategy Auction Adventure | Vibrant Colors for Two to Four Players | Family Friendly Fun by Kosmos

Magformers Magnets in Motion Set - Engineering Magnet Toys for Brain Development - 300 Pc Set I have bought three sets of magformers now for all of my grandchildren (3 to 14). Even toddlers can play with them because they are too large to swallow. They also like the solid shapes and colors of Magnatiles but those are more expensive. You can also get magnetic wooden blocks (Tegu) but those are really expensive so I haven't bought any.

The magformers are one of those toys that both kids and adults can sit and play with for an hour or longer. What I've noticed with three young grandkids together is that they each have their favorite pieces and styles of construction. One always creates vehicles, one creates houses, and the third makes towers. The colors and feel of the pieces are both soothing and exciting to work with.

Update: I had five kids and two adults playing with these recently and the person that seemed the most focused on building things is an MIT Neuroscientist. Once he built things following the guide, the kids quickly caught on and followed suit. I recommend that an adult work with the kids to begin with.

Regarding complaints about the magnets not working, if you snap together two piles of similarly shaped objects and then try to put the two piles together, sometimes the piles will reject each other. If you take one pile and start adding it to the other one at a time, all the pieces hold to each other. It seems as though the magnets must change polarity inside the plastic. I'd love a proper explanation.

I only recommend getting sets of 40 or more to have enough pieces to be creative. Wait for them to go on sale unless money is no object. Since all the grandkids took their sets home with them, I've bought a fourth set to keep at my house.

Addendum per request: I first chose these toys because of the brightly colored plastic material but soon discovered that having the pieces snap together and hold their shape is quite satisfying. While they don't take away from the joy of plain wooden blocks, they are different and allow you to vary how you play with them.

This particular kit is right for me because I'll have a crowd of five young children and many adults (thankfully two engineers) for two weeks over Christmas and I'll put this out on a large sofa table in the living room near the tree. That way the kids will feel like they have toys and waiting won't be so hard. It also incorporates many of the other kits you can buy separately so the kids can see specific types of builds.

Go to youtube and type in magformers to see how they are used. Construction is really that easy.
text_fidelity_b: Magformers Magnets in Motion Set - Engineering Magnet Toys for Brain Development - 300 Pc Set

Army Military Combat Helicopter Building Toy, City Police Helicopter Building Blocks Sets with Military Vehicle, Tank, Boat, Best Combat Roleplay STEM Toys for Boys and Girls Age 6-12 (968 Pieces) Nice, inexpensive, off-brand LEGO set that has a few small vehicles, and one large helicopter. They're nicely packed in a bucket that has a top you can use as a baseplate, but unlike a lot of other kits by this company, there are no minifigs included. It says "City Police" but this is clearly a military themed set.

Once assembled, there is no chance that you can fit a minifig into most of the small models, and it will be a tight fit for the helicopter as well, but it does work. There are some odd building choices - putting a propeller axle in the center of a larger block structure and connecting it to nothing, for example, but the models are all fairly simple and easy to build. The instructions are not LEGO quality, and the bags, while labeled, are not necessarily in order, but they are good enough for my 6 year old to do mostly on her own.
